title: The Shocking Truth of the Identity Mystery
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji made his decision, an aged sigh echoed from the depths of the Tianji Record—Mo Xiansheng seemed to want to say something, but forcefully swallowed his words back.

text.content: The Tianji Record Fragment violently trembled, golden characters scattering like startled fireflies. Chen Ji felt a sharp pain in his brow center—the connection between the Tianji Record and his soul was frantically warning him. Mo Xiansheng's voice turned sharp as iron scraping across dark iron: 'Chen Ji! Everything he says is memory manipulation! The truth from ten thousand years ago has already been erased by the Heavenly Eye—you're only seeing the illusion it wants you to see!'

Chen Ji's eyes narrowed slightly, alarm bells ringing in his heart. Mo Xiansheng had never lost his composure like this—even when facing Ling Yuan's assassination attempt, this mysterious existence who guarded the Tianji Record with a remnant soul had never shown the slightest panic. But now that urgent warning, almost cracking in pitch, was clearly born of fear—fear of the secret Cang Yutian was about to reveal. The more he was forbidden to know, the more he had to find out. 'Continue.' Chen Ji spoke calmly, his voice showing no trace of fluctuation, as if discussing today's weather.

dialogue.content: Upon hearing this, Cang Yutian let out a low laugh. That laughter carried no emotion whatsoever, yet it caused the temperature of the entire space to drop by three degrees. 'A remnant soul guardian? You think it's your master?' He raised his hand and traced a mysterious rune in the air. 'It's merely a monitoring program left by the previous master of the Tianji Record—whenever the bearer deviates from the predetermined track, it jumps out to correct. The Mo Xiansheng you trust? It's nothing but a collar the Heavenly Eye has placed around your neck.'

text.content: The Tianji Record Fragment's trembling suddenly stopped. Silence. Terrible silence. Chen Ji felt Mo Xiansheng's aura seem to freeze—it offered no rebuttal. Seeing this, Cang Yutian's smile deepened: 'Now, let me tell you your true identity. You think you're the trash servant of Tianqing Sect? Think that the Tianji Record you accidentally found that night changed your life trajectory?' He walked forward slowly, each step landing on Chen Ji's heartbeat. 'Wrong. From the very beginning, you were a piece designed for a chess game—except unlike others, you are a descendant of the Chess Player.'

A majestic force erupted from the depths of Chen Ji's bloodline. He looked down at his hands—golden patterns were faintly emerging beneath his skin, like the veins of mountains and rivers, and also resembling the trajectories of some ancient formation. At the same time, a blurry image forcibly flooded into his mind: high above the endless sky, a white-robed man played chess against the Heavenly Eye, the gameboard displaying the birth and death of countless stars. That man's face... was seven-tenths similar to his own!

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian watched the golden patterns emerging beneath Chen Ji's skin, a complex emotion flickering in his eyes—that was the wariness of meeting one's own kind, but also the weariness spanning long ages. 'Ten thousand years ago, the Heavenly Eye wanted a piece that could carry the Tianji Record. It selected a mortal family, offering the promise of immortality in exchange for them serving as containers for the Tianji Record generation after generation. Your ancestors agreed, and thus you were born—Chen Ji, or rather, you should have been the seventeenth generation inheritor of the 'Chess Player'.'

text.content: Chen Ji felt his blood boiling. Every inch of his bones felt like being scorched by flames, yet his expression remained as calm as still water—this was the achievement of his years of cultivation: even if the heavens collapsed and the earth cracked, there would be no trace of emotion on his face. He calculated rapidly in his heart: if what Cang Yutian said was true, then Mo Xiansheng's stance warranted reexamination; if false, why would the other party go to such great lengths to set up this scheme to this point? Whether true or false, he had to extract maximum benefit from this conversation.

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian suddenly reached out, a golden light shooting into Chen Ji's brow center. In that instant, scenes from ten thousand years ago flickered past like a carousel: a young man kneeling before the Heavenly Eye making a blood oath, vowing to guard the Tianji Record until its completion; a woman fleeing pursuers with an infant in her arms, behind her a burning clan ancestral hall; an old pair of hands hiding the Tianji Record Fragment in a baby boy's swaddling clothes... that was Chen Nian! His sister! Why would her infancy appear in a scene from ten thousand years ago?

text.content: The torrent of memories stopped abruptly. Chen Ji knelt on one knee, cold sweat soaking his back. Cang Yutian looked down at him from above: 'Seen clearly now? This is the destiny flowing in your bloodline. You think you're worthless? That was a seal set by the Heavenly Eye to prevent your premature awakening. You think you stumbled upon fortune? The Tianji Record chose you only because of the contract—your ancestor's blood letter from ten thousand years ago.' He paused, 'And your sister Chen Nian, is the final key prepared by the Heavenly Eye for this generation.'

choice.prompt: Cang Yutian's words struck his heart like heavy hammers. Chen Ji felt something within him loosening—the bloodline power sealed for seventeen years, or the self-understanding he had always firmly believed in. Faced with this truth sufficient to overturn everything, he had to make a choice...

choices.description: Since the bloodline is so, since fate is so, then accept it calmly—follow the trend and transform this destiny into the sharpest sword in your hands.
choices.risk_hint: May Be Completely Controlled by the Heavenly Eye

text.content: Chen Ji slowly stood up, a faint smile curling at the corner of his lips. 'Since the bloodline is so, since fate is so—' He raised his hand, allowing the golden patterns to spread beneath his skin. 'Then I shall follow the trend.' The words fell, the seal within his body shattered with a thunderous crash, and a majestic force so overwhelming it stole one's breath poured from his dantian, washing through his limbs and bones. This was the power of the Chess Player's bloodline—never successfully awakened by anyone in ten thousand years.

choices.description: Truth often hides in the details—he wanted to question those illogical gaps, piecing together the real answer from fragments.
choices.risk_hint: May Miss the Full Picture of the Truth

text.content: Chen Ji did not respond immediately. He lowered his eyes in contemplation for a moment, his fingertips lightly tapping his thigh—a habitual action when he was thinking. 'A contract from ten thousand years ago,' he raised his gaze, a sharp light flickering in his eyes, 'since it's a contract, there should be two parties. You say my ancestors made a pact with the Heavenly Eye—then who was the other party to that contract? It couldn't have been you, Cang Yutian, could it?' His lips curved slightly. 'Or could it be... that you're also just a piece being used?'

choices.description: To hell with bloodline destiny—he, Chen Ji, only believes in his own calculations, and every fate must be broken by his own hands.

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly burst out laughing. That laughter was clear and bright, echoing through the dead-silent space. 'A descendant of the Chess Player? A Heavenly Fate key?' He brushed the non-existent dust from his robe. 'Cang Yutian, you've said so much—do you have even a shred of evidence?' He looked around. 'Scenes from ten thousand years ago? The power of bloodlines? Who's to say you didn't fabricate all this to trick me into your scheme. This Chen Ji acts only on what his own eyes see and his own calculations.' Before the words even finished, the Tianji Record suddenly hummed—as if responding to his will.

Cang Yutian's smile froze for a moment. He stared at Chen Ji, as if seeing this ant-like human truly for the first time. 'Interesting.' He spoke slowly. 'I've seen too many people whose throats were gripped by destiny—some wept and pleaded, some begged and wailed, some went mad... yet never have I seen one who, having glimpsed destiny's shackles, could still laugh like this.' He stepped back, the golden light around him gathering inward. 'It seems you truly are different from others. Very well, let's end today's session—if you want to know more, go find your sister.'

The space began to distort. Chen Ji felt a gentle yet irresistible force pushing him outward. He instinctively tried to grab something, only to find Cang Yutian's form dissolving. 'Wait—' He opened his mouth, only to find his voice suppressed by some force. Cang Yutian's final words drifted into his ear: 'Remember, the more complete the Tianji Record becomes, the closer you are to death. If you're smart enough, you'll keep it incomplete forever—unfortunately, smart people often die the earliest.'

When Chen Ji opened his eyes again, he found himself still standing at the Cliff Edge of Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. The evening breeze brushed his face, moonlight shone like water, as if that earth-shaking conversation had merely been a dream. But the burning sensation in his palm reminded him—everything was real. He looked down at the Tianji Record Fragment, golden characters slowly circulating, among which a line of text he had never seen before had appeared: 'The blood of the Chess Player can reverse heaven, or it can shatter heaven.'

Just then, a familiar fragrance drifted over. Su Qingyao's figure emerged from the shadows of the trees, moonlight illuminating her cold features. 'Just now there was a strange phenomenon at the Back Mountain, and I sensed the Tianji Record's energy fluctuation.' Her gaze was like a sword, piercing directly toward Chen Ji. 'What have you been hiding from me again?' Chen Ji raised his eyes to meet those scrutinizing eyes, a meaningful curve forming at the corner of his lips. Mo Xiansheng's warnings, Cang Yutian's revelations, his sister Chen Nian's connections—these mysteries
